scenario: AITA for giving my girlfriend pointers on how to cook better? | So my girlfriend is pissed at me and has a cooking "strike" because, and I quote,"if you are so much better than me at cooking you can do it yourself". We moved in together 6 months ago (been together for 2 before it) and we came to an agreement that she will do the cooking since she comes 2h earlier from work and I was all on board for having a hot meal ready when I come home. The thing is she is not exactly good at it. She isnt terrible, everything she makes is edible but is far off from the standard I was used to. So, I started to give her pointers. After all she cant get better if she doesnt know that something is off. I would tell her whenever she used too little salt or too much spice, if something was a little burnt or undercooked, told her when I knew how to make the dish better next time etc. I would always eat all of it and say thank you so it was not like I was being rude about it. The thing is that she "snapped" when my mother came to visit and I casually said that she could give my girlfriend some cooking advice. My girlfriend nodded and smiled and generally seemed fine in the moment but as soon as the doors closed behind my mother my girlfriend went ballistic, accused me of humiliating her and her cooking in front of my family and stormed off. Since then I apologised saying that I am sorry for giving her constructive criticism in front of my mom but it didnt calm her much and she still refuses to make anything food-related at home for me. I think she is overreacting, I never complained about her cooking or throw it out. I was just being helpful. I miss her cooking, not gonna lie, so I might as well ask here if I stepped over the line somewhere. AITA or is my girlfriend crazy?

Let's think about this. On one hand, he was trying to help her improve her cooking skills. He provided constructive criticism, and he did it in a way that wasn't overtly rude—he always ate everything and thanked her. That seems like a good intention. He wanted her to get better so that she could feel more confident in her cooking, and he wouldn't have to adjust as much to a lower standard. On the other hand, the girlfriend felt humiliated, especially when his mom was involved. It's possible that she felt that her cooking skills were being judged not just by him but by his family, which added pressure. Even if he didn't mean to embarrass her, the way he brought up the idea in front of his mom might have made her feel insecure or criticized. Another angle is the dynamic of the relationship. They had an agreement that she would cook because of her schedule. If he's constantly pointing out improvements, it might feel like he's not fully respecting her role or her efforts. It could come across as him not appreciating what she does, even if he doesn't mean it that way. Also, the girlfriend's reaction might be about more than just the cooking. It could be about feeling undermined or not supported. When he suggested his mom give advice, it might have felt like he was bringing in someone else to fix the problem, which could make her feel like he doesn't trust her or value her efforts. So, while his intentions were good, the way he delivered the feedback and the context in which he did so might have been insensitive. He didn't consider how she might feel about receiving criticism, especially in front of his family. It's possible that he overstepped by not being more mindful of her feelings and the potential impact of his words. In conclusion, while he didn't mean any harm, the way he approached giving feedback and involving his mom might have been inappropriate. He should have been more considerate of her feelings and perhaps discussed the feedback in a more private and supportive manner.
